Three dog cots were identified with chewed and jagged edges. Jagged plastic edges can be sharp and can potentially
cause injury. In addition, jagged and worn edges cannot be effectively sanitized. All surfaces of housing facilities including
furniture-type objects must be replaced when worn. The facility must correct this issue.
*******Corrected at the time of inspection on September 8, 2026

The Program of Veterinary Care for dogs had not been signed by the current attending veterinarian. The plan had been
previously approved by the former AV, however it had not been updated to reflect the change. The PVC for dogs must be
approved and signed by the current Attending Veterinarian for the facility. The facility must correct this issue.
********Corrected on September 14, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture

Mailstop #3W11
